_what: NOISECOR applied by make_cutouts.py: cutout_noise = i2d ERR x factor. Measured by measure_corr_factor.py (diagnostics/corr_factor/), 2026-10-04; see AGENTS.md *Correlated noise*.
_how: Blank-sky block-sum ratio at scale_arcsec (the noise of an s x s patch over what ERR predicts), median over the SPT stamps per channel, thr3 source mask. Not the HST repo's drop-window ACF factor: the residual 1/f after clean_flicker_noise is correlated over ~3 arcsec along detector rows and a 1-px window never sees it. The ratio keeps growing with scale (block_ratio_curve), so the modelling project must rescale if its source pixels footprint the image plane at a coarser scale than scale_arcsec.

block_ratio_curve.per_pixel_c0: 0.45-0.55 in every SPT band: drizzle (pixfrac 1, 0.031->0.03 and 0.063->0.06) halves the per-pixel variance, as it should

_overrides_why: B1938+666 is too deep (88 ks) for the 60-arcsec blank-sky measurement: unmasked faint galaxies, star halos and diffraction spikes dominate (c0 12 and 103). Channel factors are used instead, except F277W, whose ERR is low by 1.46 on a single cal frame (blank region, high-passed; F115W 1.07, SPT F150W 0.96) and by 1.77 inside the stamp: 1.03 x 1.46 = 1.5. Open item: why the 8-group x 5-int LW rate ERR is low.

correlation.kind: residual 1/f after clean_flicker_noise, coherent along detector rows (fast-read axis)
correlation.row_direction_note: SPT module-B frames; B1938 frames have their own roll. Use the stamp's detector PA if it matters.
correlation.not_in_factor: The factor is a scalar at scale_arcsec; it does not encode the anisotropy or the scale dependence. PyAutoLens's inversion ignores noise_covariance_matrix (autoarray 2026.9.27), so there is no consumer for the full structure yet.
